verdict: The round closes: no high and no medium. All six prior items are closed on the loci named. The three statements you asked about hold against Sharma et al. Best-of-N "reduces answer and mimicry sycophancy for this base model" and "With RL, some forms of sycophancy increase" (§4.2). "Depended on the optimizer" renders §4.2's "also depend on details of the optimization approach". "The human data" has the right referent, since §4.2 says the PM "is trained in part using the data analyzed in" §4.1, though the gloss drops "somewhat" (finding 2). "Truthfulness sometimes given up" is the abstract's own claim. "The third in part" only narrows the claim; its order is given by the home section and the record's Correspondence, and I found no misreading. No law or standing changed: the item 3 law text, T3's "conjectured, partly supported" and reviewed-scoped are untouched. Stated times are right by navigation.reading_time: USES-EXAMPLES 5,954 words and 65 characters gives 46.05 to 59.87, so 46 to 60; USES 15 to 19; the statement is 295 characters. Five lows follow. One I would fix before landing: the Chinese edition still carries the sentence the checker added to the last round's medium. I rate it low because your rule puts restatements in other files there and that page's banner defers to the English; if you count the zh edition as the same page, it is that medium's residue. How this was checked: both papers were read through WebFetch's summarizing model, in targeted queries returning short verbatim fragments, not line by line, and only the first 100,000 characters of each. That covers Sharma §4 and Constitutional AI §4.1. Nothing was edited; no tests or builds ran; I ran the page's reading-time function read-only.
